fields.Name: Triads
fields.Summary: Three books sharing a connection that can be named precisely, read from their own files, with verified quotations, a constellation diagram, notebook prompts, rabbit holes, a Lexicon term and a line to carry. Volume 1 of the Scribrarium (32 triads, 96 books).
fields.Procedure: The full instructions of the daily scheduled task as run on 2026-10-25 are kept in the Triomnibus repository at method/triads_prompt_v1.md. Outline: preflight on the Mac (Scribrarium mounted read-only); load the Calibre catalogue; avoid repeats via the Books table; read the Lexicon; draw ~150 random candidates and hunt two companions by targeted searches; state the link in two sentences and rate difficulty 1-5; read each book from its own file and verify every quotation by substring check with a location; write up (Thread, constellation, three book sections with at least two elements each, Where this sends you, From the Lexicon, To carry); deliver PDF to Drive, Google Doc, Grist Sets/Books rows and the Lexicon update; verify.
fields.Sources: Commonplace-book practice: Ann Blair, Too Much to Know (Calibre 5817).
fields.Notes: Retired for now on 2026-10-26, not abandoned; can be rotated back in.

fields.Name: An author and their shadow
fields.Summary: One author per week. Day 1: the author's own work. Days 2-6, through the library's full-text index: who quotes them, who argues with them, who translates or rewrites them, who uses them without credit (recorded as suspicion), and a second own work read in the light of the week. Day 7: the map of who cites whom on Johnny's own shelves.
fields.Procedure: Full text in the Triomnibus repository at method/shadow_prompt_v0.3.md; identical to the daily scheduled task's instructions as switched on 2026-10-25 (night). v0.2 changed author selection to the queue; v0.3 added STEP 1c, the complete capture of every book mentioning the author into the Mentions table. Records: Sets (Method, Author_Week, Week_Day), Books, Shadow_Edges, Mentions, Author_Weeks.
fields.Sources: Calibre full-text index (12,819 formats indexed, 2026-10-25). Moretti, Network Theory, Plot Analysis (Calibre 5420) and Hage & Harary, Structural Models in Anthropology (9870) for the network idea.
fields.Notes: First author: Elias Canetti (chosen 2026-10-25; Kathy Acker deferred to a later week). Hardest category: uncredited use; treated as suspicion with evidence, never as finding.

fields.Name: Lens and specimen
fields.Summary: A week with one book about reading; each day one of its procedures applied to a single book, with a note on what the procedure found and what it missed.
fields.Sources: Sedgwick, Touching Feeling (12221); Felski, The Limits of Critique (9618); Guillory, On Close Reading (9586); Barthes, The Pleasure of the Text (500); Eve, Close Reading with Computers (3802).

fields.Name: News oracle
fields.Summary: One concrete phrase from the previous day's news, searched across the library's full text; the book chosen is the one that illuminates it from the greatest distance in time or field, not the one that merely mentions it.
fields.Sources: Sortes Vergilianae (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sortes_Vergilianae); Adam Smyth, 'pins through paper' (https://adamsmyth.substack.com/p/pins-through-paper).

fields.Name: Margin and Lexicon
fields.Summary: Start from one of Johnny's Calibre highlights or a Lexicon term and trace its occurrences through the library with verified quotations; verified finds can be written back to the Lexicon as checked attestations.
fields.Sources: Ann Blair, Too Much to Know (5817).

fields.Name: Mnemosyne panel
fields.Summary: Five to nine short passages from as many books sharing a gesture or form, arranged without a stated thesis, plus one line naming the gesture. Variant: deformance (reading backwards, nouns only, WordNet substitutions).
fields.Sources: Warburg, Bilderatlas Mnemosyne: The Original (6173); Warburg Institute virtual exhibition (https://archive.warburg.sas.ac.uk/aby-warburg-bilderatlas-mnemosyne-virtual-exhibition); Ramsay, Reading Machines.
